title: Compression Error Sensitivity Analysis for Different Experts in MoE Model Inference
problem: Serving large Mixture of Experts models under GPU memory constraints requires offloading non-activated experts. Expert offloading between GPU and main memory creates data transfer bottlenecks that must be addressed via compression.
motivation: Understand how compression-induced errors in different experts affect MoE inference accuracy to enable efficient selective compression.
method: When serving Mixture of Experts models on GPUs with memory constraints, unused experts must be transferred between GPU and main memory frequently, creating a data transfer bottleneck. To reduce this, the approach uses error-bounded lossy compression—specifically the SZ3 and CuSZp algorithms, which shrink data by accepting a controlled amount of intentional information loss. The researchers then systematically measure how these compression errors affect the model's inference accuracy across different layers of the network.
key_novelty: Different layers in Mixture of Experts models tolerate compression errors with varying robustness—some can withstand aggressive compression while others are highly sensitive.
contributions: Application of error-bounded lossy compression to MoE expert offloading
Comprehensive analysis of layer-dependent compression error sensitivity
Discovery that shallow/deep layers tolerate compression while middle-layer experts are sensitive
Practical guidance for selective compression in MoE inference
key_findings: Shallow-layer experts: minimal accuracy degradation with bounded errors
Middle-layer experts: significant accuracy loss with bounded errors (critical)
Deep-layer experts: bounded errors can improve accuracy (instruction following optimization)
limitations: Limited to SZ3 and CuSZp compression algorithms. Specific MoE models and benchmarks not detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: Compression Error Sensitivity in MoE Model Inference
